newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Tesco checks in robust sales.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Tesco checks in robust sales.

text.p: Britain's leading supermarket chain Tesco sent its shares to new highs on Monday after posting robust Christmas sales, prompting analysts to wonder whether arch-rival J. Sainsbury may have been left in its wake.
In what it called "another excellent trading period", Tesco said like-for-like sales grew 7.5 percent in the five weeks over Christmas and New Year, while total sales jumped 12.2 percent.
In the 21 weeks to January 5, like-for-like sales rose by 8.1 percent and total sales surged 13.1 percent.
Chairman Lord MacLaurin said the supermarket group's sales continued to outperform the industry average.

"This illustrates the increased attractiveness of Tesco to customers and the outstanding commitment of all our people. We look forward to reporting another good set of results in April," he said in a statement.

Analysts welcomed the figures which came in at the top end of expectations. But while Tesco's shares rose, J. Sainsbury saw its stock fall 5.5 pence to end at 391p ahead of its own trading statement, due on Friday.

"At first glance, the market will obviously think that if Tesco is doing well then they must be hurting somebody -- and that somebody is Sainsbury," said Bill Myers, food retail analyst at brokers Williams de Broe.
But he added: "I think Sainsbury's figures will also be OK, but not as good as Tesco's."

Tesco, whose shares ended two pence higher at 369p after hitting a high of 373p, said its performance was the result of its trading strategy of "investing in low prices" after the launch of its Unbeatable Value campaign last September.
Tesco also said its product range and customer service approaches had borne fruit.
The company's Clubcard loyalty scheme had continued to grow in popularity and in November it awarded 56 million pounds ($94 million) worth of vouchers and money-off coupons to customers.
Smaller supermarket group Budgens Plc also reported higher sales in the 28 weeks to November along with strong half year results, on Monday.
But the firm added that, as usual, it had failed to benefit from the kind of bumper growth enjoyed by its giant rivals.

Sales rose by 8.1 percent to 183.0 million pounds, while on a like-for-like basis they climbed 4.5 percent. Budgens, which plans to open 10 new stores this year, said half-year pre-tax profits rose by 18 percent to 5.04 million pounds.
Budgens shares ended 1/4p lower at 46.5 pence. ($1=.5979 Pound)
